name: ISNA
description: ISNA returns TRUE if the supplied value is the #N/A error, and FALSE for any other value or error.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The value, cell reference, or formula result to test.

basicExample.explanation: NA() returns the #N/A error, which ISNA detects.

advancedExamples.title: Trap a missing VLOOKUP
advancedExamples.scenario: Return a friendly message when a lookup fails.
advancedExamples.description: Replace #N/A with text using IF and ISNA
advancedExamples.formula: =IF(ISNA(VLOOKUP("x", A2:B10, 2, FALSE)), "Not found", VLOOKUP("x", A2:B10, 2, FALSE))
advancedExamples.explanation: When the lookup returns #N/A, ISNA is TRUE and the formula shows "Not found".

advancedExamples.title: Other errors are not #N/A
advancedExamples.explanation: 1/0 produces #DIV/0!, which is not #N/A, so ISNA returns FALSE.

howItWorks: ISNA returns TRUE only when the value is exactly the #N/A error. Other error values (#VALUE!, #REF!, #DIV/0!, #NUM!, #NAME?, #NULL!) and normal values all return FALSE. It is commonly paired with IF to handle lookup misses gracefully.

howToSteps.name: Build the lookup
howToSteps.text: Write the formula that may return #N/A.

howToSteps.name: Review
howToSteps.text: When #N/A occurs, the fallback value appears.

limitations: Detects only #N/A; use ISERROR for all error types.
Does not catch #N/A produced indirectly unless the error cell is referenced.
Returns FALSE (not an error) for ordinary values.

commonErrors.error: Using ISNA to catch every error
commonErrors.fix: Use IFERROR or ISERROR to handle all error types.
Prefer IFNA or IFERROR, which evaluate once.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: ISNA works identically in Google Sheets with the same syntax and behavior.

faq.question: ISNA vs IFNA?
faq.answer: IFNA replaces only #N/A with a value; ISNA only tests and returns TRUE/FALSE.

faq.question: Does ISNA catch #VALUE!?
faq.answer: No, only #N/A returns TRUE; other errors return FALSE.

faq.question: When is #N/A returned?
faq.answer: Typically by lookup misses in VLOOKUP, HLOOKUP, MATCH, XLOOKUP, or by the NA() function.
